text: Inuktitut. Early forms. Proto-Eskimo–Aleut.Inuktitut: [inuktiˈtut], syllabics ᐃᓄᒃᑎᑐᑦ[note 1]), also known as Eastern Canadian Inuktitut, is one of the principal Inuit languages of Canada.

title: Inuktitut, Eastern Canadian | Ethnologue Free
text: Eastern Canadian Inuktitut is an endangered indigenous language of Canada. It belongs to the Eskimo-Aleut language family and is part of the Inuktitut macrolanguage. The language is used as a first language by all adults in the ethnic community, but not all young people.

title: Eastern Canadian Inuktitut / Nanavik Inuttitut
text: Eastern Canadian Inuktitut has a vigesimal system with special substructures for numbers 6 to 9. However, in everyday, even monolinguals in Inuktitut, they now count in English, except for figures 1 to 5 and, sometimes, number 10.
